home.eyebrow: Built on the Web Crypto API
home.title: Cryptography, inside your browser.
home.lead: Encryption, signing and hashing happen right on this page. Your text, files and private keys are never sent to any server.
home.why.title: Why you can trust it
home.why.local.title: Data stays on your device
home.why.local.text: The page's security policy (CSP) blocks the browser from sending requests anywhere. It is not just a promise; the browser enforces it.
home.why.std.title: Standard algorithms
home.why.std.text: No home-made crypto: AES-GCM, RSA-OAEP, ECDSA and SHA-2 come from the browser's built-in Web Crypto API.
home.why.open.title: Open source
home.why.open.text: All of the code is on GitHub, and every tool has a "How it works" panel that explains each step.
footer.note: Started as a project for an Information Security and Cryptography course. For learning purposes; it has not had an independent security audit.

encrypt.lead: Encrypt text or a file with a password. Nobody can open the package without the password; you can decrypt it with the same password.
how.title: How it works
encrypt.how.1: A 256-bit AES key is derived from your password with PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) and a random 16-byte salt. The iterations slow down password guessing; the salt makes the same password give a different key every time.
encrypt.how.2: The data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and a random 12-byte IV. Besides encrypting, GCM produces a 16-byte authentication tag: if even one bit of the package changes, decryption is refused.
encrypt.how.3: The version, iteration count, salt and IV are written at the start of the package and included as "additional data" (AAD), so they cannot be changed either. The password and the key are never in the package.
encrypt.how.4: Decryption runs the same steps backwards: the salt and iteration count are read from the header, the key is derived again and the tag is checked. A wrong password and a modified package look the same; in both cases the tag does not match.
encrypt.how.warning: If you lose the password there is no way to recover the data; the password is not stored anywhere.

rsa.lead: Generate a key pair: share the public key, keep the private key. Data encrypted with the public key can only be decrypted by the holder of the private key.
rsa.keys.title: Key pair
rsa.keys.warning: Never share the private key. This page does not store the keys anywhere; download them before closing it.
rsa.bench.title: Encrypt or decrypt
rsa.publicHint: The key you generated above is filled in automatically; you can also paste someone else's public key.
rsa.privateHint: You need the private key that belongs to the public key the package was encrypted with.
rsa.how.1: RSA is a key pair: data encrypted with the public key can only be decrypted with the private key. Its security rests on how hard it is to factor the product of two large primes.
rsa.how.2: RSA can only encrypt a few hundred bytes at a time and is slow. So every message gets a random AES-256 key, the data is encrypted with AES-GCM, and RSA-OAEP encrypts ("wraps") only that AES key. This is called hybrid encryption; HTTPS and PGP work the same way.
rsa.how.3: OAEP is the padding scheme that adds randomness to RSA: the same key encrypting the same message twice gives different output, and the old "textbook RSA" attacks no longer work.
rsa.how.4: The fingerprint is the SHA-256 hash of the public key. When you receive someone's public key, confirm the fingerprint with them another way (phone, in person) so you would notice if someone in between handed you their own key.
rsa.how.warning: The private key is downloaded as an unencrypted PEM. In real use, keep it somewhere safe (e.g. a password manager).
js.done.generate: The {0}-bit key pair is ready and has been filled into the fields below.
js.done.rsaEncrypt: Encrypted. Only the holder of the private key can decrypt this package.
js.err.noPublicKey: Paste a public key or generate a key pair above.
js.err.pem: Could not read the key: paste it completely, including the -----BEGIN ... KEY----- lines. Check that the public and private keys are not swapped.
js.err.keyType: This key is the wrong type for this operation: the RSA page expects an RSA key, the signature page a P-256 (ECDSA) key.
js.err.keyWeak: This key is too short; it must be at least 2048 bits.
js.err.wrongKey: This package was encrypted for another public key; this private key cannot decrypt it.
js.err.tampered: The package was modified; the encrypted data could not be verified.
sign.lead: Sign text or a file with your private key. Anyone with your public key can verify that the data was not changed and that it came from you.
sign.keys.title: Signing key pair
sign.bench.title: Sign or verify
sign.how.1: First the SHA-256 digest of the data is computed; the signature covers this 32-byte fingerprint rather than the data itself. That is why a 1 KB text and a 1 GB file are signed equally fast.
sign.how.2: The private key signs the digest with ECDSA on the P-256 curve. Every signature uses a random number, so signing the same data twice gives two different signatures; both are valid.
sign.how.3: The verifier hashes the data again and checks the signature with the public key. If a single byte of the data changed, or the signature was made with another key, verification fails.
sign.how.4: A signature does not keep the data secret: the data stays readable, only its integrity and origin are proven. If you also need secrecy, encrypt the data as well.
sign.how.warning: Invisible differences in text (a trailing space, line endings) also break the signature. The signature uses the 64-byte r‖s format, which differs from OpenSSL's DER format.
js.done.generateEc: The P-256 key pair is ready and has been filled into the fields below.
js.done.sign: Signed. Send the signature with the data; the recipient can verify it with your public key.
js.verdict.validText: The data has not changed since it was signed, and it was signed by the owner of this public key.
js.verdict.invalidText: The data was changed, the signature was made with another key, or the signature does not belong to this data.
js.err.noSignature: Paste the signature to verify or load it from a .sig file.
js.err.signature: Could not read the signature: a 64-byte ECDSA P-256 signature (Base64) is expected.
js.err.emptySignText: Enter the text to sign or verify.
hash.lead: Compute the SHA-256 and SHA-512 hashes of text or a file, check whether a download matches its published hash, or produce an HMAC with a secret key.
hash.expectedPlaceholder: e.g. the SHA-256 published on a website
hash.expectedHint: Case, spaces and colons do not matter; SHA-256 or SHA-512 is detected from the length.
hash.how.1: A hash function turns data of any size into a fixed-size fingerprint: 32 bytes for SHA-256, 64 bytes for SHA-512. The same data always gives the same hash.
hash.how.2: Changing even a single bit gives a completely different hash (the avalanche effect). The data cannot be recovered from the hash, and finding two inputs with the same hash is practically impossible. That is why hashes are used to check that downloads are intact.
hash.how.3: HMAC mixes a secret key into the hash. Without the key nobody can change the data and produce a valid HMAC, so it is used to verify API requests and webhooks. Simply hashing "key + data" is not safe; HMAC's construction closes that weakness.
hash.how.4: The comparison runs in constant time: it does not stop at the first different character, so the time taken does not reveal how much of the value was right.
hash.how.warning: SHA-256 is not suitable for storing passwords: it is so fast that it does not slow down guessing. Passwords need slow functions such as PBKDF2, bcrypt or Argon2 (the Password encryption tool uses PBKDF2).
js.verdict.matchText: The data is identical to the value you compared with; it has not changed.
js.verdict.noMatchText: The data is different or the value belongs to something else. If this is a download, do not use it; download it again.
js.err.expectedFormat: The value to compare does not look like a SHA-256 (64 characters) or SHA-512 (128 characters) hash.
js.err.hmacKey: Enter a secret key for the HMAC.
